```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

# Data Science: Into the Tidyverse

![](https://imageio.forbes.com/blogs-images/insertcoin/files/2018/12/spider4.jpg?format=jpg&height=600&width=1200&fit=bounds)

This data set contains information on all of the Marvel Comics. Much like Miles Morales cleans up the NYC streets, transforms into Spiderman, and assesses villains, we can use tidyverse functions to clean, transform, and assess the data. The tidyverse contains 8 libraries which are foundational to data science work in R:

- ggplot2: Data visualization
- dplyr: Data manipulation
- tidyr: Neaten messy data
- readr: Read in data
- purrr: Functional programming
- tibble: Data frame
- stringr: String manipulation
- forcats: Factor work

# Load Data
```{r load-data}
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jocslater-code/DATA607/refs/heads/main/tidyverse/Marvel_Comics.csv"
comics_raw <- read_csv(url)  
glimpse(comics_raw)
```

# Data Cleaning
```{r data-cleaning}
# Replace "Free" with 0 in price
comics_clean <- comics_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Price_numeric = case_when(
      tolower(Price) == "free" ~ 0,
      tolower(Price) == "none" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(gsub("[$,]", "", Price))
      )
  )
# Extract year
comics_clean <- comics_clean %>%
  mutate(
    parsed_date = mdy(publish_date),
    pub_year = year(parsed_date)
  ) 
# Remove year one because that doesn't make sense
comics_clean <- comics_clean %>%
  filter(between(pub_year, 1939, 2026))
```

# Analysis
```{r basic-analysis}
# Create a price summary over time
price_summary <- comics_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(pub_year), !is.na(Price_numeric)) %>%
  group_by(pub_year) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_price = mean(Price_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_price = median(Price_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
    issue_count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Visualize Results
```{r visualize}
# Plot the price summary
ggplot(price_summary, aes(x = pub_year, y = mean_price)) +
  geom_line(color = "#E23636", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#202020", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Comic Book Price Over Time",
    x = "Publication Year",
    y = "Average Price ($)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  )
```
